gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 1?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 1 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from multiple models positions 25°C as the most probable daily maximum for Munich on September 2, 2026, with 26°C a close secondary outcome.** Short-range guidance, including GFS-based outputs and European sources such as Meteoblue and Yr.no, shows afternoon peaks of 24–26°C under partly to mostly cloudy skies. High pressure associated with an Azores high extension maintains a moderate westerly flow of Atlantic air, limiting both strong warming and significant cloud cover that would suppress temperatures.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from multiple models positions 25°C as the most probable daily maximum for Munich on September 2, 2026, with 26°C a close secondary outcome.** Short-range guidance, including GFS-based outputs and European sources such as Meteoblue and Yr.no, shows afternoon peaks of 24–26°C under partly to mostly cloudy skies. High pressure associated with an Azores high extension maintains a moderate westerly flow of Atlantic air, limiting both strong warming and significant cloud cover that would suppress temperatures.

Observed model agreement is tight for this 24-hour lead time, with limited spread reflecting typical uncertainty ranges in boundary-layer mixing and insolation under variable cloud. Historical climatology for early September (average high ~22°C) provides context that current conditions sit modestly above normal but well below record levels. No major forecast shifts have occurred in the past 24–48 hours, supporting the market-implied odds that heavily favor 25°C while assigning meaningful but secondary probability to 26°C. Updated model runs and official DWD guidance expected overnight will be the next key inputs for any probability adjustment.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office and model guidance for September 2 point to a mostly cloudy day with southwesterly flow, light morning rain risk, and afternoon brighter spells that limit surface heating. Official forecasts converge on a maximum of 21–23 °C, with many runs peaking near 21 °C under widespread cloud and modest wind speeds that enhance mixing and suppress further warming. Early-September climatology places the London mean daily maximum near 20–22 °C, so current conditions align closely with the seasonal norm rather than any anomalous ridge or warm advection. Updated model runs released overnight on September 1 reinforced the 21 °C outcome as the modal solution, prompting the market’s heavy weighting toward that bin while leaving modest probability for a 22 °C nudge if afternoon sun breaks through more than expected. No major forecast shifts have occurred in the past 24 hours to alter this consensus.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from sources including WeatherBug and WindBorne currently project a high of 83–84°F for New York City on September 3, 2026, with a 70–90% chance of showers or thunderstorms, southwest winds of 5–10 mph, and high humidity.** This aligns closely with the market’s leading outcomes (84–85°F at 35.5%, 86–87°F at 20.5%, and 82–83°F at 20%), which together capture over 75% of trader-implied probability.

The primary scientific drivers include an incoming warm, moist air mass ahead of a weak frontal boundary. Southwest flow advects humid air from the south, supporting surface temperatures in the low-to-mid 80s, while widespread cloud cover and precipitation reduce solar insolation and cap daytime heating near or slightly above the seasonal average high of 80.2°F. Model consensus shows limited spread, with most runs clustering in the 82–85°F range; any breaks in clouds or delayed rain could push readings toward 86°F, while heavier or earlier precipitation would favor the lower end of that band.

Recent observations from September 2—persistent rain, highs only in the mid-70s, and dew points near 70°F—reinforce the setup for continued warmth without extreme heat. Traders appear to be weighting the latest model runs and official guidance (NHC/NOAA analogs for early-September patterns), producing tight clustering around the most probable temperature bins rather than outliers. Updated forecast packages expected overnight or early on September 3 represent the next key data point that could shift these implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from sources including WeatherBug and WindBorne currently project a high of 83–84°F for New York City on September 3, 2026, with a 70–90% chance of showers or thunderstorms, southwest winds of 5–10 mph, and high humidity.** This aligns closely with the market’s leading outcomes (84–85°F at 35.5%, 86–87°F at 20.5%, and 82–83°F at 20%), which together capture over 75% of trader-implied probability.

The primary scientific drivers include an incoming warm, moist air mass ahead of a weak frontal boundary. Southwest flow advects humid air from the south, supporting surface temperatures in the low-to-mid 80s, while widespread cloud cover and precipitation reduce solar insolation and cap daytime heating near or slightly above the seasonal average high of 80.2°F. Model consensus shows limited spread, with most runs clustering in the 82–85°F range; any breaks in clouds or delayed rain could push readings toward 86°F, while heavier or earlier precipitation would favor the lower end of that band.

Recent observations from September 2—persistent rain, highs only in the mid-70s, and dew points near 70°F—reinforce the setup for continued warmth without extreme heat. Traders appear to be weighting the latest model runs and official guidance (NHC/NOAA analogs for early-September patterns), producing tight clustering around the most probable temperature bins rather than outliers. Updated forecast packages expected overnight or early on September 3 represent the next key data point that could shift these implied probabilities.

This consensus, combined with observed midday readings near 31°C and limited cooling from scattered showers, underpins the market’s strong weighting toward 31°C as the most probable outcome. Lower probabilities for 30°C or 32°C reflect minor model spread in boundary-layer mixing and precipitation timing, while extremes above 33°C or below 29°C remain unlikely given stable large-scale conditions and historical early-September climatology. Traders appear to be pricing in official guidance updates through the afternoon observation window.

eventMetadata.context_description:

Hourly model outputs and station guidance peak in the low 20s °C during the afternoon before temperatures ease overnight.

These conditions reflect typical early-September synoptic setup: a broad area of low pressure to the west steering relatively cool, moist maritime air across southern England, suppressing strong daytime heating. Light rain or drizzle risk in the morning further limits insolation, while breezy southwest winds (gusts to 25–30 mph) enhance mixing and prevent localized warming. Historical averages for the date at London Heathrow sit around 21.6°C, providing climatological context that aligns with current model consensus.

No major shifts in guidance have occurred in the past 24 hours, keeping market-implied probabilities heavily weighted toward 21°C (61.5%) and nearby outcomes. Model spread in afternoon cloud cover and timing of any breaks creates the tight 25 °C versus 26 °C contest reflected in market-implied odds, with resolution hinging on the precise peak observed by official stations.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Cloud cover, easterly flow, and high humidity are suppressing daytime heating in New York City on September 2, 2026, keeping the maximum temperature in the low-to-mid 70s and aligning with the market’s leading 74-75°F bin (42.5% implied probability) followed by 72-73°F (24.5%).**

Official forecasts from the National Weather Service and multiple models (including GFS runs) show mostly cloudy skies with only a slight afternoon shower chance, limiting solar insolation and preventing temperatures from reaching the late-summer climatological average high near 80°F. Persistent onshore easterly winds (5–10 mph) advect cooler, moist marine air, while dew points in the upper 60s further cap the diurnal rise. Early-morning observations confirm overcast conditions and light rain, consistent with model consensus that the day’s peak will occur in the 72–75°F range rather than the warmer outcomes priced lower in the market.

No significant forecast shifts have occurred in the past 24–48 hours, and resolution will hinge on the official highest reading at a primary NYC station (typically Central Park). Traders are weighting the stable, cooler pattern heavily, which explains the tight clustering around mid-70s outcomes.

Afternoon temperatures in hourly guidance peak around 21°C before easing, reflecting the influence of an unsettled early-autumn air mass rather than any strong warming ridge.

These conditions align with typical early-September climatology for southern England, where average highs hover near 18–20°C but can reach the low 20s under similar synoptic setups. The absence of clear skies or warmer advection keeps probabilities concentrated on 21°C (59.5% implied), with 20°C and 22°C as the nearest alternatives. No extreme heat or rapid model shifts have emerged in the latest runs to push odds significantly higher or lower. Traders are weighting the consensus of national forecasting agencies, which emphasize gradual afternoon improvement but no substantial temperature rise.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover, northeasterly winds, and a moist air mass are suppressing daytime heating in New York City on September 2, 2026, keeping official forecasts centered on a high in the low to mid-70s. Multiple model runs and NWS guidance project peak temperatures near 72–74°F under overcast skies with a slight chance of light showers, well below the late-summer climatological average of roughly 80°F. This setup reflects a cooler-than-normal post-frontal regime rather than any strong warming advection. Market-implied odds heavily favor the 72–75°F range because recent observations and updated model consensus show little potential for significant afternoon clearing or southerly flow that could push readings higher. Final resolution will hinge on the official maximum recorded at Central Park or equivalent NWS stations.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the National Weather Service and major ensembles indicate NYC highs on September 3 will likely fall in the mid-80s, with the tight 36%–35% split between 86–87°F and 84–85°F reflecting small but meaningful differences in projected 850-hPa temperatures, boundary-layer mixing, and the timing of any onshore flow or cloud cover. A persistent ridge and light southerly winds favor modest warmth above seasonal normals, while any strengthening sea breeze or subtle shortwave could cap readings one to two degrees lower. Historical early-September climatology shows highs averaging near 81°F, so current guidance places this day several degrees above baseline. Updated model runs and the NWS forecast discussion tomorrow morning represent the key data releases that could shift the narrow market consensus before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble models indicate a maximum of 30–32°C for Tokyo on September 3 amid increasing cloud cover, southeasterly flow, and 40–60% precipitation chances from scattered showers or thunderstorms. These conditions reduce insolation and promote evaporative cooling relative to clearer prior days, aligning with climatological September normals near 29–30°C. Trader consensus on 31°C and 32°C as frontrunners reflects model agreement on modest daytime warming before rain arrives, while lower probabilities for 29°C or below account for residual uncertainty in timing of cloud build-up and any localized clearing. Updated model runs and JMA briefings through early September 3 will refine these ranges ahead of market resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent National Weather Service and private model consensus points to a high of 84°F in Central Park on September 4, 2026, under mostly sunny skies after northwest winds clear morning moisture.** This follows showers and thunderstorms on September 3 that leave behind drier air, with highs forecast in the mid-80s across the metro area.

September climatology supports this range: the 1991–2020 average high is 80°F, and recent years have frequently reached the low-to-mid 80s on this date. The current setup features post-frontal subsidence, modest dew points, and clear conditions that favor efficient daytime heating without excessive humidity or cloud cover suppressing temperatures.

The market’s heavy weighting on the 84–85°F bin (44.5%) reflects this tight forecast cluster, while lower probabilities on 82–83°F and 86–87°F account for typical model spread and minor urban heat-island variability. No significant warm or cool anomalies are expected to shift the outcome outside the mid-80s before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Cloud cover, easterly onshore flow, and modest moisture are capping temperatures in New York City today, aligning closely with the market’s heaviest weighting on 72–75 °F.** Official National Weather Service forecasts and real-time model guidance (including GFS-based products) call for a mostly cloudy day with highs in the mid-70s, peaking near 72–76 °F under light northeast-to-east winds of 5–10 mph. These conditions limit solar heating while drawing cooler marine air from the Atlantic, a typical late-summer pattern that suppresses afternoon maxima relative to the seasonal average high of ~80 °F.

Recent observations reinforce this outlook. Yesterday’s high reached 82 °F under clearer skies; today’s increased cloudiness and 20 % chance of light showers have already trimmed expected warming. Dew points in the upper 60s add humidity that further moderates surface temperatures. With the day well underway and no signals of clearing or stronger southerly flow that could push readings into the upper 70s or beyond, the market’s implied probabilities—led by 74–75 °F at 45.5 % and 72–73 °F at 28 %—reflect the narrow, observationally supported range. Higher bins (76 °F+) carry sharply lower odds consistent with the limited upside in current guidance.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Cloud cover, easterly onshore flow, and modest moisture are capping temperatures in New York City today, aligning closely with the market’s heaviest weighting on 72–75 °F.** Official National Weather Service forecasts and real-time model guidance (including GFS-based products) call for a mostly cloudy day with highs in the mid-70s, peaking near 72–76 °F under light northeast-to-east winds of 5–10 mph. These conditions limit solar heating while drawing cooler marine air from the Atlantic, a typical late-summer pattern that suppresses afternoon maxima relative to the seasonal average high of ~80 °F.

Recent observations reinforce this outlook. Yesterday’s high reached 82 °F under clearer skies; today’s increased cloudiness and 20 % chance of light showers have already trimmed expected warming. Dew points in the upper 60s add humidity that further moderates surface temperatures. With the day well underway and no signals of clearing or stronger southerly flow that could push readings into the upper 70s or beyond, the market’s implied probabilities—led by 74–75 °F at 45.5 % and 72–73 °F at 28 %—reflect the narrow, observationally supported range. Higher bins (76 °F+) carry sharply lower odds consistent with the limited upside in current guidance.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and multiple models indicate widespread cloud cover, frequent showers, and thunderstorms over Tokyo on September 4, driven by a strengthening frontal system and northeasterly flow that limits daytime heating and solar insolation. These conditions are expected to cap the daily maximum well below early-September climatological normals near 29–30 °C, positioning 26–28 °C as the most probable range and explaining the market’s heaviest trading around 27 °C (35.5 %) and 26 °C (23.5 %). Persistent high humidity and moderate winds further reduce the likelihood of brief clearing that could allow brief spikes toward 29 °C or higher, while the same moisture supports the low single-digit probabilities assigned to outcomes below 24 °C. Updated model runs and official briefings through September 3 will provide the next key data points for refining these implied probabilities.

Model consensus shows little spread, with peaks concentrated in the mid-afternoon before cooling overnight. Recent short-range updates have remained stable, reinforcing trader confidence in the narrow 24–26°C band while assigning very low probability to extremes outside 23–27°C. Resolution will depend on the official Munich station reading (typically the daily maximum at the primary observing site), with any last-minute model shifts or unexpected cloud cover the primary variables that could nudge the outcome within the favored range.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) and supporting models position 30–32°C as the most probable range for Tokyo’s daily maximum on September 3, 2026.** 

The JMA’s September 2 update calls for a mostly cloudy day with rain developing later, especially from midday onward, and assigns a 30°C maximum (some local media citing 31°C). Multiple private forecasts converge on highs of 28–31°C (roughly 82–88°F), with afternoon showers and thunderstorms limiting peak heating. Southerly flow ahead of an approaching front maintains moisture and cloud cover, while the timing of precipitation reduces insolation during the warmest hours. 

This setup follows a warm September 2 (observed max near 32–33°C) and aligns with early-September climatology, where daily normals sit around 29–30°C but convective activity frequently caps extremes. Model consensus shows limited upside beyond 32°C once rain begins, while downside below 29°C would require earlier or heavier precipitation than currently indicated. The market’s heavy weighting on 30°C (23.5%) and 31°C (36.0%), followed by 32°C (22.0%), directly reflects this narrow forecast envelope and the modest uncertainty around exact rain onset and intensity. Updated JMA or numerical guidance in the next 12–18 hours will be the key catalyst for any shifts in implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast consensus from numerical weather models positions 25°C as the leading outcome for Munich’s September 3 high, with 24°C and 26°C close behind.** Multiple sources, including DWD-MOS, ECMWF, GFS, and Yr.no runs, converge on a peak of 24–26°C under partly cloudy skies, moderate westerly winds of 10–18 km/h, and surface pressures near 1022–1023 hPa that support gradual daytime heating without strong advection. This range sits above the 1991–2020 climatological average high of ~22°C yet remains well below extreme records, reflecting stable late-summer conditions rather than anomalous warmth. Recent model updates show minimal spread and no major shifts in the synoptic pattern, giving traders high confidence in the narrow 24–26°C band while assigning only low probability to outliers.

gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 4?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current ensemble forecasts from sources including the German Weather Service (DWD) and global models show Munich under high pressure with mostly clear skies and light westerly winds on September 4, supporting peak afternoon temperatures of 27–30 °C after morning lows near 16–18 °C. Differentiation between the closely matched 29 °C and 30 °C outcomes hinges on subtle variables such as exact boundary-layer mixing, minor cloud reductions in solar insolation, and model spread in maximum heating rates under light winds, all within the typical uncertainty of short-range temperature predictions near the seasonal average high of 21.6 °C.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current ensemble forecasts from the Met Office and ECMWF indicate a Friday maximum near 22–23 °C for London, driven by strengthening westerly winds, increasing cloud cover, and scattered showers that limit solar heating and enhance mixing.
